description: The provided image displays three bar charts, labeled (a) WikiText, (b) PTB, and (c) C4, each comparing the perplexity of two methods—“Uniform” (blue bars) and “Ours” (orange bars)—across different quantization bit settings (3, 4, 8, and 16 bits) on their respective datasets. In each chart, the horizontal axis represents “Quantization Bits,” with the bars grouped by bit value, and the vertical axis represents “Perplexity,” scaled linearly. Chart (a) WikiText uses a y-axis ranging from 0 to 30, chart (b) PTB ranges from 0 to 400, and chart (c) C4 ranges from 0 to 30. For each quantization level, two bars are shown side-by-side: the blue “Uniform” bar and the orange “Ours” bar. In chart (a), the “Uniform” perplexity values are approximately 30, 27, 26, and 26 for 3, 4, 8, and 16 bits respectively, while the “Ours” values are approximately 22, 19, 18, and 18. In chart (b), the “Uniform” values are approximately 400, 320, 300, and 300, and the “Ours” values are approximately 250, 180, 180, and 180. In chart (c), the “Uniform” values are approximately 30, 25, 25, and 25, and the “Ours” values are approximately 21, 19, 18, and 18. The bars are not sorted and are consistently grouped by quantization bit, with no visual emphasis beyond color coding. The charts do not include error bars or statistical annotations.
